artists.biography: Anneke van Giersbergen (born March 8, 1973) was the singer in the Dutch band The Gathering from 1995 to 2007 when she announced her departure, summer 2007. She has since formed Agua de Annique with whom she released new songs in the fall of 2007. She has also worked with Devin Townsend Project, Danny Cavanagh & Anathema, Lawn, The Farmer Boys , Ayreon, Napalm Death, Globus, Moonspell, Giant Squid, Novembers Doom, Wetton/Downes, Maiden United and she has also done a live guest performance for Within Temptation. Her new album "The Darkest Skies Are The Brightest" is out now. Dianne van Giersbergen and Anneke van Giersbergen are both Dutch symphonic metal singers with the same last name. They are not related, but share a common last name, which is also the name of a small village in the Netherlands. They are both known for their strong vocal abilities and have achieved notable success in the symphonic metal scene. Read more on Last.fm. perplexity.description:
Everything Is Changing" is Anneke van Giersbergen's solo studio album released in 2011, marking a significant departure from her work with The Gathering. The album showcases a blend of alternative rock and pop rock, demonstrating van Giersbergen's versatility as a vocalist and songwriter beyond her progressive metal roots. With a runtime of 45 minutes, the record presents a more accessible and introspective sound compared to her band's heavier material, featuring tracks like "Feel Alive," "You Want To Be Free," and the title track "Everything Is Changing."

The album represents an important moment in van Giersbergen's solo career, allowing her to explore a broader sonic palette while maintaining the emotional depth characteristic of her vocal performances. Released on Agua Recordings, the project reflects her artistic evolution during a period of personal and professional transition. The work established her credibility as a solo artist capable of crafting compelling material outside the progressive rock framework for which she is best known, contributing to her growing reputation as a multifaceted musician willing to experiment across different genres and styles.
